test_cases.title: Register Application With Fixed Period
test_cases.setup: Initialize a JUNO_SCH_T scheduler root using caller-provided storage. Prepare a mock application with a start hook, a periodic hook, and a configured period of 10 ms.
procedure: Call JunoSch_RegisterApp() with the scheduler root, the mock application, and period=10 ms.
Capture the returned status code.
Query the scheduler for the registered application count.
Inspect the registered period associated with the mock application.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: JunoSch_RegisterApp returns JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS, the registered app count increments by one, and the stored period equals 10 ms.

test_cases.title: Register Multiple Applications With Distinct Periods
test_cases.setup: Initialize a scheduler root with capacity for at least three applications. Prepare three mock applications A, B, C with periods 5 ms, 50 ms, and 500 ms respectively.
procedure: Register application A with period 5 ms.
Register application B with period 50 ms.
Register application C with period 500 ms.
Query each registered app's period from the scheduler.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All three registrations return JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS and the stored periods match 5 ms, 50 ms, and 500 ms respectively.

test_cases.title: Reject Registration After Initialization Complete
test_cases.setup: Initialize a scheduler root and register one mock application. Call the scheduler's initialization-complete entry (e.g., first JunoSch_Run cycle or JunoSch_Start) so the schedule is finalized.
procedure: Confirm the scheduler reports an initialized/started state.
Attempt to register a new mock application with period 20 ms.
Capture the returned status code.
Query the registered application count.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: JunoSch_RegisterApp returns a non-success status (e.g., JUNO_STATUS_ERR) and the registered app count is unchanged.

test_cases.title: Periodic Invocation At Registered Period
test_cases.setup: Initialize a scheduler root with a fake/monotonic time source under test control. Register a single mock application with period 10 ms whose periodic hook increments a call counter.
procedure: Start the scheduler.
Advance the fake time source by 100 ms while invoking the scheduler tick.
Read the mock application's call counter.
Repeat for a 200 ms advance and read the counter again.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: After 100 ms, the periodic hook has been invoked exactly 10 times; after 200 ms total, exactly 20 times.

test_cases.title: Distinct Periods Drive Distinct Invocation Rates
test_cases.setup: Initialize a scheduler root with a fake time source. Register app FAST at period 5 ms and app SLOW at period 500 ms; each periodic hook increments its own counter.
procedure: Start the scheduler.
Advance the fake time source by 1000 ms while invoking scheduler ticks.
Read the FAST and SLOW counters.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: FAST counter equals 200 (1000/5) and SLOW counter equals 2 (1000/500) after 1000 ms of simulated time.

test_cases.title: Deterministic Invocation Order Across Cycles
test_cases.setup: Initialize a scheduler root with a fake time source. Register three applications A, B, C all at period 10 ms; each periodic hook appends its own ID to a shared trace buffer.
procedure: Start the scheduler.
Advance the fake time source so the scheduler runs at least 5 cycles where all three apps are due.
Capture the contents of the trace buffer.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The trace buffer contains the same fixed sub-sequence (e.g., [A, B, C]) repeated identically on every cycle where all three apps are due.

test_cases.title: Scheduler Continues After Application Failure
test_cases.setup: Initialize a scheduler root with a fake time source. Register apps A and C with passing periodic hooks (period 10 ms each) and app B (period 10 ms) whose periodic hook always returns JUNO_STATUS_ERR. Each app has a call counter.
procedure: Start the scheduler.
Advance the fake time source by 100 ms.
Read counters for A, B, and C.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Counters for A, B, and C each equal 10 after 100 ms; the scheduler does not abort, panic, or skip A and C when B returns an error.

test_cases.title: Start Hook Invoked Once Before First Periodic Invocation
test_cases.setup: Initialize a scheduler root with a fake time source. Register a mock application with period 10 ms whose start hook increments a start counter and whose periodic hook increments a tick counter and asserts that start_count >= 1.
procedure: Start the scheduler.
Advance the fake time source by 50 ms.
Read the start_count and tick_count.
Restart the fake time source for an additional 50 ms; read counters again.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: start_count equals 1 after the first cycle and remains 1 after subsequent cycles; tick_count is greater than zero and the start-before-tick assertion never fires.

test_cases.title: POSIX and Pico2 Equivalent Invocation Sequence
test_cases.setup: Build the SCH library for both POSIX and Pico2 targets. Configure a fixture that registers identical apps A, B, C (periods 5 ms, 10 ms, 50 ms) and records the invocation sequence to a serial/log buffer. Run the same fixture under each build with a fake time source advanced by 100 ms.
procedure: Run the POSIX fixture binary; capture the recorded invocation sequence to posix_seq.log.
Run the Pico2 fixture (or its host-replay equivalent); capture the recorded invocation sequence to pico2_seq.log.
Diff posix_seq.log against pico2_seq.log.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The two invocation sequence logs are byte-identical across the 100 ms simulation window.

test_cases.title: Compile-Time Capacity Bound Enforced
test_cases.setup: Configure the scheduler with a compile-time capacity macro JUNO_SCH_MAX_APPS=4. Initialize a scheduler root sized to that capacity. Prepare five mock applications with period 10 ms each.
procedure: Inspect libjuno/include/juno/sch/juno_sch_api.hpp to confirm the capacity is a compile-time constant (e.g., template parameter, constexpr, or macro) with no dynamic resizing API.
Register applications #1 through #4 and capture each return status.
Attempt to register application #5 and capture the return status.
Query the registered application count after step 3.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Inspection confirms a compile-time capacity bound; registrations 1-4 return JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS, registration 5 returns a non-success status, and the registered count is exactly 4.

test_cases.title: Caller-Owned Storage And No Dynamic Allocation
test_cases.setup: Build the SCH library against a POSIX harness that overrides ::operator new, ::operator new[], malloc, calloc, and realloc to fail or assert. Provide a caller-owned JUNO_SCH_T storage buffer and an array of caller-owned application slots.
procedure: Inspect libjuno/include/juno/sch/juno_sch_api.hpp and libs/sch_lib/src/**/*.cpp to confirm no calls to malloc/calloc/realloc/new/new[] exist in library code.
Initialize the scheduler root using caller-provided storage.
Register four mock applications using caller-provided slots.
Run the scheduler for 100 ms of fake time.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Source inspection finds no dynamic allocation calls; the harness reports zero allocations during init, registration, and 100 ms of execution.

test_cases.title: Reject Registration With Period Outside Supported Range
test_cases.setup: Initialize a scheduler root using caller-provided storage. Prepare mock applications configured with periods 5 ms, 500 ms (boundary cases) and 0 ms (invalid).
procedure: Register a mock application with period 5 ms; capture the status.
Register a mock application with period 500 ms; capture the status.
Attempt to register a mock application with period 0 ms; capture the status.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Registration at 5 ms and 500 ms return JUNO_STATUS_SUCCESS; registration at 0 ms returns a non-success status.
